metaDescription: Six 24 inch washer-dryer combos compared on ventless vs vented drying, wash and dry capacity, cycle times, pet cycles and the tower alternative.
expertTake: The COMFEE' 2.7 cu ft combo is the best overall pick because it pairs a 26 pound wash capacity with steam care and an overnight wash-and-dry cycle at a modest price tier. The Equator convertible is the pick for the rare owner who can vent, since it switches between vented and ventless drying. Anyone who regularly dries full loads of towels should skip combos and buy a separate dryer, because combo dry capacity is far below wash capacity. Prices move, so treat tiers as relative. Check the nameplate drum size before ordering.
introParagraphs: A 24 inch washer-dryer combo does both jobs in a single drum. Clothes go in dirty and come out dry, and the machine needs no vent to the outdoors, which is why combos dominate apartments, dorms and RVs.

The tradeoff is capacity and time. Wash capacity is always larger than dry capacity, drying takes hours, and a combo cannot run two loads at once. Understanding those limits is the whole job of choosing one.

products.name: COMFEE' 24 in 2.7 cu ft ventless washer-dryer combo, 26 lb
products.description:
COMFEE' offers a 2.7 cubic foot drum with a 26 pound wash capacity, a ventless dryer, steam care and an overnight wash-and-dry cycle. The steam mode refreshes clothes and helps with allergens, and the overnight cycle is the headline convenience: load it before bed and wake up to dry clothes. The no-shaking claim refers to a balanced spin that keeps vibration down.

As with every ventless combo, drying is slow and the dry load is smaller than the wash load, so wash a full drum but dry in smaller batches. It sits in the lower-middle price tier, which is attractive for the capacity. Compared with the Midea, it is a close match on specs; compared with the Equator, it has a much bigger drum.

Ownership centers on the condenser and filter. Clean the lint filter every cycle, run a tub clean monthly and leave the door ajar. Give it a cold water tap, since the condenser uses it to cool humid air. Drying small half loads gives better results than a packed drum. Many owners say the overnight cycle is the reason they chose a combo, since it removes the wet-laundry transfer.
products.bestFor: Apartments and RVs that want one machine with a big wash drum.
cons: Dry capacity far below wash capacity
Needs cold water for the condenser

products.name: Midea 24 in 2.7 cu ft ventless washer-dryer combo, 1400 RPM
products.description:
Midea markets its 2.7 cubic foot combo for families of three to four, with a 1400 RPM spin, steam care and an overnight cycle. The high spin pulls extra water out before drying, which shortens the condensing phase and saves time and energy. Midea has a long record in compact appliances, and its combos are the usual benchmark in the category.

The constraint is the same as every combo: dry capacity is smaller than wash capacity, so heavy loads will come out damp. It sits in the middle of the price range. Compared with the COMFEE', the spin speed is explicitly listed; compared with the Hamilton Beach, it has a larger quoted drum.

Ownership requires lint filter cleaning every cycle, tub cleaning monthly and a periodic look at the condenser water path. Wipe the door boot after the cycle. Its spin speed is the main reason owners report shorter drying than on slower combos.
products.bestFor: Small families that value an established compact brand.
cons: Dry load smaller than wash load

products.name: Equator 24 in 110V convertible combo, 1.6 cu ft, pet cycle
products.description:
Equator's convertible combo lets you choose vented drying for speed or ventless drying for flexibility, with a 1.62 cubic foot, 15 pound drum, a 1400 RPM spin and a pet cycle. The vented option is the big deal, because a vented dry stage is much faster than condensing and cheaper to run. The pet cycle is designed to remove hair before drying.

The small drum is the cost: it is the smallest in the group, so it suits one or two people. The vented mode needs a duct, which not every rig or apartment can provide. It sits in the upper-middle tier. Compared with the COMFEE', it is smaller but more flexible; compared with the all-in-one vented/ventless unit, it is the more established model.

Ownership requires lint cleaning and, if you vent, a duct that stays clear. Check the duct run annually. Check duct length before you plan to vent. Keep the door seal clean, because pet hair collects there and causes leaks.
products.bestFor: Pet owners and singles who may be able to vent.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER BCW27MW 2.7 cu ft combo, 16 cycles
products.description:
BLACK+DECKER's BCW27MW combines a 2.7 cubic foot drum, 16 wash cycles and a 120V ventless dryer with Auto Dry and Timed Dry modes. Auto Dry ends when the sensor says the load is done, while Timed Dry lets you control the minutes. The model requires no exhaust, so it installs anywhere with water, drain and an outlet.

It is a basic machine without steam or smart features. The drying capacity is smaller than the wash capacity, as always. It sits in the middle tier. Compared with the COMFEE', it lacks steam and an overnight cycle; compared with the KoolMore, it lists the same drum.

Ownership is routine. Clean the lint filter, wipe the door boot and run a tub clean monthly. The timed dry is useful for finishing damp items. Auto dry saves guesswork, but over-full drums still end up damp.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 2.65 cu ft combo, 26.4 lb wash, 17.6 lb dry
products.description:
Hamilton Beach publishes both numbers that matter on a combo: 26.4 pounds of wash capacity and 17.6 pounds of dry capacity, in a 2.65 cubic foot drum. That honesty shows exactly how much smaller the dry load is, about two thirds of the wash load. Four temperature options adapt to different fabrics.

The stated dry limit is a useful reminder to split large washes. It sits in the lower tier of the group. Compared with the Midea, it gives clearer capacity data; compared with the COMFEE', it lacks the steam and overnight features in the listing.

Ownership is routine. Clean the lint filter every cycle and keep the door ajar after use. Use the numbers to split big loads. It is a good reminder that capacity labels always refer to the wash side. It also lists four temperature steps.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want clear capacity numbers at a lower tier.
cons: Dry load is two thirds of wash load

products.name: KoolMore 2-in-1 2.7 cu ft combo, 16 wash and 4 dry cycles
products.description:
KoolMore offers a 2.7 cubic foot drum with 16 wash cycles, four dry cycles and a fast 20 minute wash. The quick wash is the standout for small loads, and the listing targets apartments, dorms and RVs. Four dry cycles keep drying simple.

It shares the usual combo limits and has little brand history. It sits in the lower-middle tier. Compared with the BLACK+DECKER, it adds the fast wash; compared with the Equator, it has more drum.

Ownership is routine: filter, tub clean and door ajar. Keep expectations for dry capacity modest. The fast wash makes it handy for a work shirt before the morning.
products.bestFor: Small loads and fast washes in tight spaces.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Hamilton Beach states 26.4 lb wash and 17.6 lb dry, a ratio of about two thirds. Most combos behave the same even if the listing hides it. Wash a full drum but dry in two batches, or run the overnight cycle with a half load. Heavy towels and jeans hold water, so they count more than their volume. The most common complaint about combos is damp clothes, and it almost always traces to overfilling the dry stage. Weigh a typical load once to learn your real numbers.

COMFEE', Midea, BLACK+DECKER and Hamilton Beach are ventless condensing, while the Equator can vent. Condensing dryers need cold water and take hours. Vented drying is faster but needs ducting. Condensing units also warm the room slightly, which matters in a small camper. A condenser that is scaled up also lengthens cycles, so descaling matters. Humidity from a vented dryer can also add to the room, so ventilate.

A full wash and dry on a ventless combo can take four to six hours, and the overnight cycle exists for a reason. Plan to run it while you sleep or work. It cannot wash a second load while drying the first. Night cycles shift the heat and noise to hours when you are asleep. A timed dry cycle can finish items that came out slightly damp. A full cycle also uses more water than a wash alone.

The Midea and Equator list 1400 RPM. A faster spin removes more water and shortens drying. It also shakes the floor, so level the machine well. Anti-vibration pads help on a wood floor. The heavier the drum, the more the floor flexes at spin. Level all four feet after the first fill.

Combos need a cold water tap, a drain and a 120V circuit. The Equator lists 110V. Avoid sharing the circuit with a heater or microwave. A combo draws the most power during the heating phase. Check also that the outlet can carry the load, and use a dedicated circuit if possible.

Steam on the COMFEE' and Midea refreshes clothes, the Equator has a pet cycle and the KoolMore a 20 minute wash. Pick features you will actually use. Do not pay for features you will not run. Steam is useful for refreshing clothes you do not want to wash fully.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity honesty
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored listings that state both wash and dry weight. Capacity claims drive disappointment, so honesty counts. We assumed a typical household overfills by about a third.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drying method
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated condensing, vented and convertible dryers. Drying method decides time and install. A duct is the single largest installation hurdle.

howWeEvaluated.title: Features
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited steam, pet and fast wash cycles. Features should save time.

howWeEvaluated.title: Installation
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered water, drain and power needs. Install needs matter in RVs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value
howWeEvaluated.description: We judged tiers from Hamilton Beach to Equator. The COMFEE' ranks first because it balances drum size, features and tier.

howToChoose.intro: Household size and laundry habits decide how much combo capacity you need.
Tiers are relative and move often. The lowest tier here is the Hamilton Beach.

cards.label: Ventless
cards.text: COMFEE', Midea, BLACK+DECKER and Hamilton Beach need no duct but dry slowly.

cards.label: Convertible
cards.text: Equator can vent for speed if you have a duct.

howToChoose.note: If you cannot duct, choose ventless. A duct is rarely possible in an apartment or RV, which is why ventless is the default.
howToChoose.intro: The core decision is ventless against vented drying, because it sets drying time, install difficulty and how much laundry you can really finish in a day.
Your drying habits decide whether a combo can replace a dryer. Some households live happily with an overnight cycle, others need two machines.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: 120V power, a drain, fresh water supply and a small footprint.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The KoolMore targets RV use; the COMFEE' and Midea suit larger rigs. Check the gray tank before your first load.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You may vent, pointing to the Equator, or want brand reach, pointing to the Midea. That premium buys flexibility, not capacity.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want clear numbers, pointing to the Hamilton Beach. A basic ventless combo does the job.

maintenance.why: A clogged filter lengthens drying. Pull lint by hand after each cycle.
Prevents mildew smell. Use a cleaner made for front loaders.
Trapped water breeds mold. Dry the boot folds with a cloth.
Leaks begin at clamps. Replace hoses showing cracks.
Scale slows drying. Use a manufacturer-approved descaler.

faq.q: Can a combo replace a separate dryer?
faq.a: For small households, yes. For big loads, no. Many owners add a drying rack for bulky items. A drying rack handles bulky items like blankets. A combo suits one or two people best.

faq.q: How long does a full cycle take?
faq.a: Four to six hours for a full wash and dry. Overnight cycles are common. Fast-wash cycles under 30 minutes are the exception.
Tiers run from Hamilton Beach to Equator. Prices change, so check listings. Spending more buys features and flexibility. Check listings before buying.
Not for ventless models. Only the convertible Equator can vent.
The dry load was too big. Split big washes into two dry loads. Reducing the dry load usually fixes it.

faq.q: Is it OK for an RV?
faq.a: With 120V, water and a drain, yes. Fresh water and a drain are the limiting factors.
